High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant seeks to withdraw I.A.No.3717/2024 which is third application for grant of temporary bail.
Accordingly, I.A.No. 3717/2024 stands dismissed as withdrawn.

Heard on I.A.No. 3516/2025 , which is the fourth application under Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 filed on behalf of the appellant - Narayan for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

02. Appellant stands convicted vide judgment dated 25.08.2018 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Agar District Shajapur in S.T.No.178/2018 and sentenced as under :
Sentence/ Imprisonment Fine (Rs.)

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Agar District Shajapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In lieu of fine Section 376(AB) of IPC RI for 21 years 1000/- RI for 2 years 354(A) of IPC RI for 3 years 500/- RI for 6 months 3(A)/4 of POCSO RI for 8 years 1000/- RI for 1 year 5(M)/6 of POCSO RI for 11 years 1000/- RI for 1 year 03.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he has been falsely implicated in the case.

He further submits that the FIR was registered on 29.07.2018, charge-sheet was filed on 01.08.2018,
case was committed on 06.08.2018 and the final judgment was passed on 28.08.2018.
2 CRA-6892-2018 Hence, appellant was not given proper opportunity to defend his case.

He further submits that during the pendency of the trial, appellant made an application to produce the CCTV footage of the bus stand where the incident is alleged to have taken place, but the same was not produced stating that there there was no CCTV camera.
However, in another case, the same Investigating Officer has filed the CCTV footage.

Further, Rakesh (DW-1) who is the owner of a shop in the bus stand, was a prosecution witness whose statement was recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C. but was not produced before the Court, hence, the appellant produced DW-1 as a defence witness.
Rakesh (DW-1) has deposed in favour of the appellant stating that no such incident has taken place.
There is no DNA report in the case.
Appellant has undergone 7 years of jail sentence.
Appeal is of the year 2018 and its final disposal will take considerable time.
Hence, in such circumstances, prayer is made for suspension of the jail sentence and grant of bail.

sentences.text: 04. Learned counsel for the respondent / State has strongly opposed the present application by submitting that the age of prosecutrix was below 7 years and the eye-witness Dashrath (PW-3) has supported the case of the prosecution.

05. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that the application for suspension of custodial sentence filed on behalf of the appellant deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, I.A.No.3516/2025 is allowed and the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.

It is directed that appellant - Narayan be released on bail subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 29.04.2025 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy, as per rules.
